items.title: Section: Withholding Genuine Praise from Someone Who Has Earned It

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，懷嫌恨心，他實有德不欲顯揚，他實有譽不欲稱美，他實妙說不讚善哉，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。若由懶惰、懈怠、放逸，不顯揚等，非染違犯。無違犯者，若知其人性好少欲，將護彼意；若有疾病；若無氣力；若欲方便調彼、伏彼，廣說如前；若護僧制；若知由此顯揚等緣，起彼雜染憍舉無義，為遮此過；若知彼德雖似功德，而非實德；若知彼譽雖似善譽，而非實譽；若知彼說雖似妙說，而實非妙；若為降伏諸惡外道；若為待他言論究竟；不顯揚等，皆無違犯。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who, gripped by resentment, are unwilling to acknowledge another's genuine virtue, unwilling to affirm their genuinely earned good reputation, and unwilling to praise their genuinely excellent teaching — this constitutes a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation. If mere laziness, indolence, or negligence is the cause, it is a non-tainted violation. ... There is no violation: when the bodhisattva knows the person genuinely prefers modesty and wishes to respect that preference; when the bodhisattva is ill or lacks the strength; when withholding serves as skilful means, as described more fully earlier; when it upholds the monastic community's own rule; when the bodhisattva knows that praising the person now would only provoke meaningless pride and defilement, and withholds specifically to prevent that outcome; when the apparent virtue, reputation, or eloquence is not, on genuine examination, actually real; when withholding serves to subdue genuinely harmful outsiders; or when the bodhisattva is simply waiting for the other person to finish speaking before offering praise, rather than interrupting mid-sentence.

items.title: Section: Withholding Deserved Reprimand, Punishment, or Expulsion Out of Corrupted Compassion

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，見諸有情應可訶責、應可治罰、應可驅擯，懷染污心而不訶責；或雖訶責，而不治罰、如法教誡；或雖治罰、如法教誡，而不驅擯；是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。若由嬾惰、懈怠、放逸，而不訶責乃至驅擯，非染違犯。無違犯者，若了知彼不可療治，不可與語，憙出麁言，多生嫌恨，故應棄捨；若觀待時；若觀因此鬪訟諍競；若觀因此令僧諠雜、令僧破壞；知彼有情不懷諂曲，成就增上猛利慚愧，疾疾還淨；而不訶責乃至驅擯，皆無違犯。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who see beings whose conduct genuinely calls for reprimand, formal punishment, or expulsion, yet, gripped by a corrupted mind, withhold the reprimand entirely; or reprimand but do not follow through with proper disciplinary correction; or discipline but do not follow through with expulsion when expulsion is warranted — this constitutes a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation. If mere laziness, indolence, or negligence is the cause, it is a non-tainted violation. ... There is no violation: when the bodhisattva recognises the person is simply beyond reasoning with, prone to harsh speech and deep resentment, and rightly lets the matter go rather than escalating; when waiting for a more appropriate moment; when correcting the person now would provoke open conflict or litigation; when it would cause disorder or an actual schism within the monastic community; or when the bodhisattva knows the person harbours no deceit at all, feels genuine and forceful shame at their own wrongdoing, and will swiftly and sincerely correct course on their own.

items.title: Section: Declining to Display Supernormal Powers Purely to Avoid Attracting Donors — All Forty-Three Minor Precepts Complete

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，具足成就種種神通變現威力，於諸有情，應恐怖者能恐怖之，應引攝者能引攝之，避信施故，不現神通恐怖、引攝，是名有犯，有所違越，非染違犯。無違犯者，若知此中諸有情類多著僻執，是惡外道，誹謗賢聖，成就邪見，不現神通恐怖、引攝，無有違犯。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who have genuinely accomplished various supernormal powers of transformation and manifestation, and who could rightly frighten beings who need frightening, or joyfully draw in beings ready to be drawn towards the path, yet who, purely to avoid the increased offerings and support such displays tend to attract, decline to manifest such power for either purpose — this constitutes a violation, a transgression, but it is a non-tainted violation. ... There is no violation when the bodhisattva recognises that the beings in question are deeply entrenched in wrong views, are genuinely hostile outsiders who slander the noble and the wise, and have fully committed themselves to mistaken doctrine — in which case declining to display such power to frighten or draw them in incurs no violation at all.

items.title: Section: Three Conditions That Excuse Every Precept Without Exception

items.zh: 又一切處無違犯者，謂若彼心增上狂亂，若重苦受之所逼切，若未曾受淨戒律儀，當知一切皆無違犯。
items.en: Furthermore, the conditions that excuse violation universally, across every single precept covered above, are these: when the bodhisattva's mind is genuinely and severely deranged; when the bodhisattva is overwhelmed by genuinely severe physical suffering; or when the bodhisattva has never actually received the pure precepts to begin with — in any of these three cases, one should understand that no violation whatsoever occurs.

items.title: Section: A Closing Charge to Study These Precepts With Genuine Reverence

items.zh: 復次，如是所起諸事菩薩學處，佛於彼彼素怛纜中隨機散說，謂依律儀戒、攝善法戒、饒益有情戒。今於此菩薩藏摩呾履迦綜集而說，菩薩於中應起尊重，住極恭敬，專精修學。是諸菩薩從他正受戒律儀已，由善清淨求學意樂、菩提意樂、饒益一切有情意樂，生起最極尊重恭敬，從初專精不應違犯。
items.en: Furthermore, these various matters of bodhisattva learning just described, the Buddha taught scattered throughout many different discourses, according to each audience's own capacity — organised around the precept of discipline, the precept of gathering wholesome dharmas, and the precept of benefiting sentient beings. Here in this treatise's own bodhisattva canon of foundational analysis, they have been systematically gathered and presented together; bodhisattvas should, towards this teaching, give rise to genuine reverence, abide in the deepest respect, and study it with focused, diligent effort. ... Bodhisattvas who have properly received the precepts from another, moved by a genuinely pure aspiration to learn, the aspiration for awakening, and the aspiration to benefit every being, give rise to the deepest reverence and respect, and, from the very first moment, apply themselves with focused diligence so as never to violate them.

items.title: Section: When a Precept Is Broken — The Five Categories of Offence

items.zh: 設有違犯，即應如法疾疾悔除，令得還淨。又此菩薩一切違犯，當知皆是惡作所攝，應向有力於語表義能覺能受小乘、大乘補特伽羅，發露悔滅。
items.en: Should any violation occur, it should immediately be confessed and cleared away in accordance with the proper method, so that purity is restored without delay. Furthermore, every violation a bodhisattva might commit should be understood as falling within the category of wrongdoing, and should be openly confessed and cleared before someone genuinely capable — a practitioner of either the lesser or the great vehicle able to fully grasp both the spoken words and their intended meaning.

items.title: Section: Three Grades of Violation, Three Different Paths Back to Purity

items.zh: 若諸菩薩以上品纏違犯如上他勝處法，失戒律儀，應當更受。若中品纏違犯如上他勝處法，應對於三補特伽羅，或過是數，應如發露除惡作法，先當稱述所犯事名，應作是說：長老專志！或言：大德！我如是名，違越菩薩毘奈耶法，如所稱事犯惡作罪。餘如苾芻發露悔滅惡作罪法，應如是說。若下品纏違犯如上他勝處法及餘違犯，應對於一補特伽羅，發露悔法，當知如前。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who commit any of the four root violations described earlier while gripped by intense, unrestrained affliction lose the bodhisattva precepts entirely and must take them again from the beginning. Those who commit such a violation under merely moderate affliction should confess before three or more genuinely qualified persons, following the same procedure used for confessing lesser wrongdoing: first stating clearly the name of the specific offence committed, and saying: "Venerable elder, please attend" — or "Noble one" — "I, so-named, have transgressed the bodhisattva's own code of discipline; as described, I have committed this offence of wrongdoing." For every other kind of violation, the procedure follows the same pattern used in the monastic code for confessing wrongdoing, exactly as described. Those who commit such a violation under only mild affliction, together with every other lesser violation, should confess before a single qualified person, following the same procedure just described.

items.title: Section: Confessing Alone Before No One but One's Own Resolve

items.zh: 若無隨順補特伽羅可對發露，悔除所犯，爾時菩薩以淨意樂，起自誓心：我當決定防護當來終不重犯。如是於犯還出還淨。
items.en: If no genuinely qualified person is available before whom the violation can be confessed and cleared, the bodhisattva should, at that time, generate a genuinely pure resolve and make this solemn inner vow: "I now resolve absolutely to guard myself going forward, and will never commit this offence again." In this way, the violation is fully cleared and purity is fully restored.

blocks.text: The last lighter precepts, then how offences are cleared.
Refusing to acknowledge another's genuine virtue out of resentment. Master Cháng Bǎi: but don't interrupt them by praising before they've finished.
Seeing beings who need reprimand, punishment, or expulsion, and withholding it "with a corrupted mind".
One with supernormal powers who could turn beings from wrong, but declines "purely to avoid attracting offerings": an untainted offence.
No offence, for any precept, "when the mind is genuinely deranged; when overwhelmed by severe pain; or before one has received the precepts".
"The Buddha taught these scattered through many discourses, according to each audience." One should study them respectfully. Master Cháng Bǎi: the pure wish to train fits the three storehouses.

"Every violation should be confessed and cleared at once." All count as minor wrongdoing (duṣkṛta) in monastic terms. A root violation committed in the severe grade loses the precepts, which must be taken again. A root violation under moderate affliction is confessed before three or more qualified people, naming the offence; under mild affliction, before one.
"If no qualified person is available, one generates a pure resolve and vows: I will not do this again."

quiz.q: Out of resentment, refusing to acknowledge another's real virtue, reputation, and excellent teaching — how is this judged?
quiz.why: This "constitutes a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation." Master Cháng Bǎi lists the virtues to praise: faith, discipline, learning, generosity, wisdom.

quiz.q: The English lists "knowing the person harbours no deceit… and will swiftly correct course" as a separate exemption joined by "or." How do the lectures treat it?
options: per the 《披尋記》, it must combine with the preceding considerations (waiting for the right time, conflict, disorder) — both conditions are needed; Cháng Bǎi: "no deceit" means not concealing one's faults
quiz.why: Both lectures, following the 《披尋記》, combine the last clause with the preceding considerations. Master Cháng Bǎi: not concealing one's own wrongs and honestly revealing them is "no deceit." Venerable Miào Jìng on conflict: people might come to blows or end up in court.

quiz.q: A bodhisattva with supernormal powers who, to avoid attracting donations, does not display them — how is this judged?
quiz.why: "Purely to avoid the increased offerings … this constitutes a violation, a transgression, though a non-tainted one." Master Cháng Bǎi: insufficient compassion — abandoning beings — but untainted. Venerable Miào Jìng: having become free of desire, there is no greed involved.

quiz.q: Which three conditions excuse violation across every precept?
options: severe derangement, overwhelming physical suffering, never having received the precepts
quiz.why: "When the bodhisattva's mind is genuinely and severely deranged; when overwhelmed by severe physical suffering; or when they have never actually received the pure precepts." Master Cháng Bǎi: never having received the precepts, how could one violate them?

quiz.q: The three intentions — the pure wish to train, the wish for awakening, the wish to benefit all beings — how are they matched in the lectures?
options: Cháng Bǎi, per the 《披尋記》: training-wish to restraint, awakening-wish to wholesome practice, benefit-wish to benefiting beings; Miào Jìng citing Tsongkhapa: the pure training-wish covers all three
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the pure wish to train corresponds to restraint discipline; the wish for awakening to the discipline of gathering wholesome practice. Venerable Miào Jìng, reporting Tsongkhapa: the pure wish to train includes all three disciplines.

quiz.q: Every bodhisattva violation falls into which category, and before whom is it confessed?
options: wrongdoing; before a person, Lesser or Great Vehicle, capable of understanding and receiving the confession
quiz.why: "Every violation a bodhisattva might commit should be understood as falling within the category of wrongdoing, and should be openly confessed … before someone genuinely capable," whether of the Lesser or Great Vehicle. Master Cháng Bǎi: bodhisattvas are very aware — whenever they do wrong they deeply regret it.

quiz.q: A root violation under moderate affliction is confessed before three or more persons. To what monastic offence do the lectures compare this?
options: sthūlātyaya (a gross offence), just below the first section; four make a saṅgha
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a gross offence may be called sthūlātyaya, just below the first section; four make a saṅgha, and a saṅgha procedure needs four. Venerable Miào Jìng: it should refer to sthūlātyaya.
